title: Lamar Jackson Has Realistic Chance to Return by Week 6, NBC Sports Reports
body:
Baltimore’s star quarterback Lamar Jackson is edging closer to rejoining the lineup, with head coach Jesse Minter indicating the former MVP is “definitely doing better” after sitting out the Week 5 matchup because of an ankle sprain. While the exact timeline remains fluid, medical staff and coaches now suggest Jackson has a realistic chance to suit up for the Ravens’ Week 6 contest, a development that could dramatically reshape Baltimore’s playoff trajectory.

Jackson’s injury, sustained during the loss to the Cleveland Browns, forced him to miss his first game of the season. The 25‑year‑old’s ankle was evaluated as a high‑ankle sprain, a condition that typically requires a cautious rehabilitation protocol to avoid lingering instability. Over the past week, Jackson has participated in light conditioning drills and a limited portion of the offense’s walk‑through, prompting Minter’s optimistic remarks. “He’s definitely doing better,” the coach said, adding that the team is monitoring his progress closely. The phrase “realistic chance” used by NBC Sports underscores that while there are no guarantees, the odds of his return have improved markedly compared to earlier in the week.

The potential comeback carries significant implications for both the Ravens and their upcoming opponents. Baltimore entered the bye week with a 3‑1 record, but the offense sputtered without Jackson’s dual‑threat capability, managing just 12 points against the Browns. The team’s rushing attack, which typically leans heavily on Jackson’s scramble, fell to 45 yards, while the passing game struggled to find rhythm under backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. A healthy Jackson could revive the Ravens’ balanced attack, providing a much‑needed boost to a unit that ranks near the bottom of the league in points per game when he is absent.

Analysts also point to the broader context of the AFC North race. The Steelers, Bengals and Browns are all within striking distance of the division lead, and a full‑strength Ravens squad could tilt the balance in Baltimore’s favor. Moreover, Jackson’s presence influences the defensive strategy of opponents; teams must account for his ability to extend plays with his legs, often forcing linebackers and safeties into uncomfortable coverage assignments. This duality has been a hallmark of the Ravens’ success over the past three seasons, and its absence was palpable in Week 5.

From a medical perspective, the decision to clear Jackson will hinge on his ability to bear weight without pain, maintain ankle stability during cutting motions, and demonstrate confidence in his plant‑and‑push mechanics. The team’s orthopedic staff reportedly performed a series of functional tests on Monday, including hop drills and agility ladders, all of which yielded encouraging results. However, they remain vigilant for any signs of swelling or reduced range of motion that could predispose him to a more severe setback.

Looking ahead, the Week 6 matchup against the New York Jets presents a timely test for Jackson’s return. The Jets have struggled defensively, ranking near the league’s bottom in pass defense, which could provide an ideal environment for Jackson to ease back into full competition. If he does take the field, the Ravens will likely limit his snap count initially, integrating him gradually while preserving his ankle for the grueling stretch of games that follows. Should Jackson stay healthy, Baltimore could solidify its status as a postseason contender and re‑ignite the excitement that surrounds his electrifying playmaking style. The coming days will reveal whether the “realistic chance” materializes into a decisive return that propels the Ravens back into the hunt.
